shared_elements: standing human figure carved in relief on a stone surface
vertical/columnar organisation of the carved field (text columns in A, upright figures in B)
justification: The only real correspondence is that both surfaces carry relief carving including upright human figures set against a flat prepared stone panel, with A's eroded figures apparently flanking the edges of the field; that is a generic feature shared by many traditions. B depicts a specific scene — a file of bearded men in profile in long robes and distinct headgear, one holding a shallow bowl and another laying a hand on the shoulder of the man ahead — whereas A is dominated by a large multi-line inscribed text panel with no discernible narrative or figural interaction.
